sentences.text: (SHRI WAKEEL KHAN - ADVOCATE FOR THE PETITIONER)

ORDER Assailing the order dated 03.12.2014 (Annexure P/1) passed in Criminal Revision No.325 of 2013 by the IV Additional Sessions Judge, Sagar (M.P.) whereby the application under Section 245 of the Cr.P.C. has been rejected
, the present petition has been preferred.

2. The complainant has filed a criminal complaint under Sections 294, 406, 420, 506-B of the IPC on 28.01.2005 against the petitioner as well as another accused namely Sarafat Hussain alleging that on 10.11.2000 they entered into an agreement for sale of a truck, lying in break down condition,
bearing registration no.MOD-6477 for an amount of Rs. 91,000/- with an assurance that his name will be entered as the registered owner and he will get the truck transferred in his name.
On 12.08.2003 when he approached Sarafat Hussain for delivery of the vehicle it came to his knowledge that the truck has been sold to some one else.
Thereafter some negotiation took place between the parties and it was agreed that the money will be returned back.

On 10.10.2003 when he again approached for the same, the petitioner not only refused to refund the money but also threatened him therefore, the complaint has been filed.
3.
It is pointed out that the complainant has filed a suit for recovery of 2 MCRC-2692-2015 money.
The learned Magistrate after recording the statement of the complainant under Section 200 of the Cr.P.C. on 06.06.2006 had dismissed the complaint at registration stage.
Thereafter, a criminal revision no.114 of 2006 was filed which was also dismissed on 12.07.2006.

The civil suit was partly decreed on 13.03.2007 holding that the agreement is rightless and the plaintiff (complainant) was not entitled to get the possession of the truck except entitled to recover the amount from Sarafat Hussain.

No relief was granted to the complainant therefore, just with the intention to harass the petitioner he has filed another complaint on 07.04.2007 for offence under Sections 294, 406, 420,

sentences.text:
Vide order dated 23.04.2008, the learned Magistrate has taken cognizance in the matter under Sections 406 and 420 of the IPC.
4.
It is argued that once the matter has already been decided between the parties by the civil courts and since there is no privity of contract between the complainant and the petitioner.
No cognizance in the matter could have been taken by the learned trial court.
The objection was taken by the petitioner by filing an application under Section 245 of the Cr.P.C..
The same was rejected on the ground that both the criminal and civil proceedings are different and are not binding on each other.

The revision preferred against the same was also rejected vide order dated 20.08.2013 therefore,
this petition under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. has been filed on the ground that the learned trial court should have considered the objections filed by the petitioner under Section 245 of the Cr.P.C.
as there is a series of litigation which has taken place on earlier occasion.
The civil suit claiming for recovery of the amount has already been preceded.
The aforesaid facts were not considered by the learned trial court and directly an application has been entertained.
The complainant has not placed all 3 MCRC-2692-2015 the relevant material before the learned trial court.

5. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and perused the record.
6.
The record indicates that vide order dated 20.02.2015 there is an interim order granted by this court and further proceedings of the Criminal Case No.2381 of 2008 was directed to be stayed.
The petitioner's counsel has pointed out series of litigation between the parties.
The civil suit was also preferred seeking recovery of the amount.
The same was partly decreed vide judgment and decree dated 13.03.2007 (Annexure P/6).
Earlier complaint which was filed has already been rejected by the learned trial court as well as by the revisional court.
The second revision filed over the very same relief could not have been entertained by the learned trial court therefore, there were some objections taken in terms of Section 245 of the Cr.P.C.
the same has been rejected by the learned trial court as well as by the revisional court.
The learned trial court as well as the revisional court have committed an error in not considering the objections taken by the petitioner.

The objections were to bring the correct facts before the court and to point out that on earlier occasion the similar complaint has been rejected and the civil suit for recovery has already been decreed which is clear from documents (Annexure P/6).
Under these circumstances, the impugned order dated 03.12.2014 is unsustainable.
The same is hereby set aside.
7. The learned trial court is directed to reconsider the application of the petitioner filed under Section 245 of the Cr.P.C. and thereafter proceed in the matter.
With the aforesaid observations, this petition stands disposed off.
8. Order be communicated to the learned trial court for necessary compliance.
